subject: Commit signal surgery: new definitions + roleplay practicals
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Commit signal surgery: new definitions + roleplay practicals

Team,

Two quick but important updates on forecast hygiene that we need to get live this week:

1) Definition changes (effective immediately)
   - Commit: deal has signed internal procurement, exec sponsor committed to timeline, and pricing is approved by finance. No outstanding legal redlines.
   - Best Case: all technical and commercial blockers cleared but procurement still collecting final PO; still 70%+ probability.
   - Pipeline (call it 'working'): active discussions, demos complete, still subject to technical/price approval.

Rationale: the ambiguity between Commit and Best Case is causing last-minute blowups in our Q math. We tightened the checklist so ACME-style deals don't slip between buckets.

Actions for each AE on deck this week:
- Audit any opportunity in Commit or Best Case with a close date in Oct/Nov; update stage with the new checklist tags and add a short note on which checklist item is outstanding if any.
- For deals where the customer has procurement only outstanding, move to Best Case and note expected PO date.
- For any Commit we cannot justify with the checklist, move back to Pipeline and flag in the Deal Notes.

Training and roleplay:
- Monica will run two live roleplay sessions next Tue/Wed 10:00-11:30 PT. These are hands-on: we will run mock calls and practice the questions that surface the true signal. RSVP by EOD Monday.
- Attached is the first-draft commit_playbook_v2.pdf and examples spreadsheet commit_examples_q3.xlsx. Please review before roleplay.

Operational notes:
- Karthik, can you push the tagging schema to HubSpot and add the new checklist fields?
- Marissa, please prioritize mid-market and enterprise AEs — we need consistent calibration across the team.

Why this matters for ACME (example): last week ACME was in Commit because finance verbally approved, but no signed PO existed and procurement had two outstanding terms. That ambiguity forced us to scramble. With the new checklist we avoid that kind of surprise.

Short, tactical. Thanks all — small changes but big upside to forecast confidence.

-Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Director, Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Commit signal surgery: new definitions + roleplay practicals

Marissa — good call. My short rule: if exec sponsor has NOT signed off formally (email or recorded commitment) then it cannot be Commit. If finance has approved pricing but procurement still needs to execute PO, put in Best Case and add expected PO date in the HubSpot PO date field.

I'll push the checklist fields to HubSpot now:
- commit_check_executive_signed (boolean)
- commit_finance_approved (enum: verbal/written/PO)
- commit_legal_clearance (boolean)
- expected_PO_date (date)

Examples attached (commit_examples_q3.xlsx) with three annotated opportunities including the ACME deal and a mid-market sample so you can see how I applied the rule.

Link to the playbook doc for comments: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c_commit_playbook

If no objections, I'll run a small automation this afternoon that bulk-tags deals missing expected_PO_date for follow-up.

-Karthik
Head of Sales Ops
Redwood Inference
